app.title: Research Hub
app.summary: A person names a note, describes their research topic in plain words, picks which literature databases to search and how many papers to return, then runs the search. The tool picks out key terms and builds a separate query for each database. It shows how many papers it found, the exact query it sent to each source, and a list of paper cards, each with its source, journal, year, authors, a shortened abstract and a link. Each run is saved as a note in a local notebook database. The person can download the search and its results as a Word document or view the raw JSON.

task.text: Find papers on a topic across several bibliographic databases from one plain-language description, and keep a record of the search.

data.text: Bibliographic records returned by literature database APIs, combined into one list, plus a saved note for each search run.
data.item: a paper record with title, source database, journal, year, authors, abstract and link

stage.text: scoping the literature at the start of a project, before reading and reviewing papers

mechanism.text: A form takes the topic description, source choice and result limit. When it is submitted, the tool builds a query in each database's own syntax, runs them all, and draws count metrics, the queries it used and a list of paper cards below the form. A download button and a raw JSON panel let the person take the same result away.

field.text: literature search across biomedical bibliographic databases

workflow.name: search several databases from one description and collect the hits

steps.here: type a note name and describe the research focus in plain words or keywords; both are required before a run goes ahead

steps.step: choose where to search and how much to return
steps.here: pick all three sources, a single one, or Europe PMC + OpenAlex, and set the maximum number of papers per source with a slider from 1 to 20

steps.step: turn the description into a query for each source and run it
steps.here: stop words are removed to get key terms; the top four are ANDed and the rest ORed, using [Title/Abstract] tags for PubMed, TITLE/ABSTRACT fields for Europe PMC and a plain keyword string for OpenAlex; if a query returns nothing, the raw text is searched instead; the queries actually sent are shown in an expander

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: one list of paper cards, each with a coloured source badge, title, journal, year, up to seven authors, a clipped abstract and an Open paper link
each run is saved as a note in a local SQLite notebook with the focus, the sources searched, the hit count and the first hit as the primary reference; the app reports the saved note and the counts
download a Word .docx with the query settings, the query sent to each source, a summary and every paper; or open the raw output JSON

distinctive: one plain-language description is turned into a separate query in each database's own syntax, and the query sent to each source is shown
if the built query returns nothing, the search falls back to the raw description
OpenAlex abstracts are rebuilt from their inverted word index, and all abstracts are cut to a fixed length
every search is saved as a named note in a lab-notebook database, with the first hit kept as the primary reference
